title: Fear of Evil Deeds
note: He defines this as being afraid to do what is sin. The chapter gathers up and forbids all the sins of the body, so it follows the chapter on useless words.

couplets.plain: Those who do evil don’t fear the arrogance called evil deeds. The worthy do.
couplets.pm: Those with evil deeds behind them don’t fear the delusion called evil deeds, because long practice has made it easy. The excellent, who have none behind them, fear it, because they have never done it.
couplets.note: செருக்கு is pride. He reads it as delusion.

links.quote: don’t fear the arrogance called evil deeds. The worthy do
links.reason: Fearing evil deeds is what separates the worthy from those who do them.

couplets.plain: Evil things breed evil, so evil should be feared more than fire.
couplets.pm: People do evil deeds expecting pleasure, but later these bring only suffering. So fear them more than fire. Fire can’t go on burning you in another time, another land or another body.

links.quote: evil should be feared more than fire

couplets.plain: They say the highest of all wisdom is to do no evil even to those who hate you.
couplets.pm: The good say that the highest of all understanding that seeks your own good is to do no evil even to those who hate you. If you could do it and don’t, you have worked out that no suffering will come to you.

links.quote: do no evil even to those who hate you

couplets.plain: Don’t plot another’s ruin, even in a moment of forgetting. If you do, righteousness will plot yours.
couplets.pm: Don’t even by forgetting think of a deed that would ruin another. If you do, the god of righteousness thinks of one that will ruin you. It plots as you plot, so however slow you are, it gets there first. Its plotting means resolving to leave you to perish. Even to think of evil is wrong.

links.quote: Don’t plot another’s ruin, even in a moment of forgetting

couplets.plain: Don’t do evil because you are poor. If you do, you will be poor again.
couplets.pm: Don’t think “I am poor” and do evil to others to end it. If you do, you will be poor again, and that evil will make you poor birth after birth. Some read it as poverty not only of wealth but of good qualities and good deeds.

links.quote: Don’t do evil because you are poor
links.reason: Poverty is no shelter: evil done in its name only makes you poor again.
Answers the plea of being short of money: the wrong only brings the want back.

couplets.plain: If you don’t want painful things to strike you down, don’t do evil things to others.
couplets.pm: Whoever doesn’t want the sins that bring suffering to come after them and torment them must do no evil deed to others. If you do, those sins will certainly strike you.

links.quote: don’t do evil things to others

couplets.plain: However fierce the enemy, people may escape. The enemy that is your own deed never goes away. It follows you and kills.
couplets.pm: Even people with the greatest enemy escape it somehow. The enemy that is an evil deed isn’t like that. It never leaves, goes wherever you go, and kills.

links.quote: The enemy that is your own deed never goes away

couplets.plain: The ruin of those who do evil is like a shadow that never leaves, and stays at their feet.
couplets.pm: The ruin of those who do evil to others is like a person’s shadow, which stretches far yet never leaves, and comes back to rest at their feet. He rejects the reading that the shadow is evil hidden in the soul until its time comes: the words say it stays at the feet, not that it vanishes.

links.quote: like a shadow that never leaves
links.reason: Ruin stays as close to those who do evil as a shadow stays at the feet.

links.quote: The ruin of those who do evil

couplets.plain: If you love yourself, don’t go near evil deeds at all, however small.
couplets.pm: If you love yourself, do no evil deed to others, however small. Deeds are of two kinds, good and evil, so he says “the evil kind”. Evil done to others brings suffering to you, which is why he appeals to love of yourself.

links.quote: If you love yourself, don’t go near evil deeds at all

couplets.plain: Know that ruin is rare for anyone who doesn’t stray aside to do evil.
couplets.pm: If someone doesn’t leave the straight path for the crooked one and do evil to others, know that they have rare ruin. “Rare” here means none.

links.quote: doesn’t stray aside to do evil
links.reason: Refusing to turn aside to do evil is what keeps a person safe from ruin.
